title: Why the December 2014 Kelantan flood was so severe (JPS explanation to Parliament)
chunk: In a written parliamentary reply in March 2015, the government summarised the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) explanation of the December 2014 Kelantan flood. JPS telemetry showed that most river levels in Kelantan rose above their danger levels. Extreme, widespread and continuous rain fell for ten days, from 15 to 24 December 2014: about 944 mm, roughly 30% of Kelantan's average annual rainfall of around 3,000 mm, in just those ten days. JPS listed five contributing causes: the extreme rainfall itself, which it linked to climate change; ground already saturated, so rain became surface runoff instead of soaking in; loss of forest buffer zones through planned and unplanned development; spring tides at the same time, which held back floodwater at the coast; and low, flat land close to fast-flowing rivers, which left many homes exposed.

title: Punca banjir besar Kelantan Disember 2014 (jawapan Parlimen)
chunk: Dalam jawapan bertulis Parlimen pada Mac 2015, kerajaan menjelaskan dapatan Jabatan Pengairan dan Saliran (JPS) tentang banjir Kelantan Disember 2014. Menurut stesen telemetri JPS, kebanyakan aras air sungai di Kelantan naik melebihi paras bahaya. Hujan lebat yang luas dan berterusan turun selama sepuluh hari, dari 15 hingga 24 Disember 2014, berjumlah kira-kira 944 mm, iaitu sekitar 30% daripada purata hujan tahunan Kelantan yang lebih kurang 3,000 mm. JPS menyenaraikan lima punca: hujan luar biasa yang dikaitkan dengan perubahan iklim; tanah yang sudah tepu sehingga hujan menjadi air larian permukaan; kemusnahan zon penampan hutan akibat pembangunan terancang dan tidak terancang; air pasang besar pada masa yang sama yang menahan aliran banjir ke laut; dan kawasan rendah serta rata berhampiran sungai deras yang mendedahkan banyak kediaman kepada banjir.

title: Upstream peaks: Sg. Galas at Dabong and Sg. Lebir at Tualang, 24 Dec 2014
chunk: A USM presentation reproduces the JPS record of the highest water levels between 1 December 2014 and 10 February 2015. On the two main upstream tributaries, both gauges went far beyond their danger levels on 24 December 2014. Sungai Galas at Dabong (normal 28 m, alert 32 m, warning 35 m, danger 38 m) peaked at 46.47 m at 16:00 on 24 December, about 8.5 m above danger. Sungai Lebir at Tualang (normal 23 m, alert 27 m, warning 31 m, danger 35 m) peaked at 42.17 m at 06:00 on 24 December, about 7 m above danger. The Lebir peaked about ten hours before the Galas. Both rivers join the Sungai Kelantan at Kuala Krai, which is why the town flooded so badly the following day.

title: Main-channel peaks: Kuala Krai (Tangga Krai), Guillemard Bridge and Kota Bharu, 25–26 Dec 2014
chunk: According to the JPS highest-water-level record reproduced in a USM presentation, the flood peak travelled down the Sungai Kelantan over about two days. At Tangga Krai, Kuala Krai (normal 17 m, alert 20 m, warning 22.5 m, danger 25 m), the river reached 34.17 m at 15:00 on 25 December 2014, more than 9 m above danger. Further downstream at Jambatan Guillemard (normal 10 m, alert 12 m, warning 14 m, danger 16 m), it peaked at 22.74 m at midnight on 26 December. At Tambatan DiRaja in Kota Bharu (danger 5 m) the peak was 6.89 m, also at midnight on 26 December. The timing shows the core MonsoonWatch idea: upstream peaks on 24 December gave roughly one to two days of warning for Kuala Krai and Kota Bharu.

title: Sungai Golok peaks in December 2014: Jenob and Rantau Panjang
chunk: The JPS record reproduced in a USM presentation shows the Sungai Golok, on the Malaysia–Thailand border, rising above its danger levels during the 2014 flood season. At Rantau Panjang (normal 5 m, alert 7 m, warning 8 m, danger 9 m) the river peaked at 10.84 m at 11:00 on 18 December 2014, much earlier than the Sungai Kelantan main channel. Upstream at Jenob (alert 21.5 m, warning 22.5 m, danger 23.5 m) the recorded peak was 24.93 m; the date in the table appears garbled. The Sungai Semerak at Pasir Puteh peaked at 2.67 m on 18 December, just below its 3 m danger level. Because the Golok flooded a week before the main channel, Pasir Mas and Rantau Panjang faced an earlier and separate wave of flooding.

title: Daily rainfall pattern, 20–25 December 2014
chunk: A daily rainfall table in a USM presentation on the 2014 Kelantan flood shows how the rain built up over six days. Summed across the listed rain stations, daily totals were 747 mm on 20 December, 1,189 mm on 21 December, 2,161 mm on 22 December (the peak day), 1,120 mm on 23 December, 1,362 mm on 24 December, and only 188 mm on 25 December, a combined 6,767 mm. Single stations recorded up to 478 mm on 22 December and 515 mm on 23 December, extreme daily totals for any location. The heaviest rain fell on 22–23 December, one to two days before the upstream rivers peaked on 24 December and the main channel at Kuala Krai peaked on 25 December. That lag from rain in the hills to the river peak downstream is what an early-warning system can use.

title: Impacts and lessons from the 2014 Kelantan flood (USM presentation)
chunk: A USM presentation on water supply during the 2014 floods summarises the impacts as 21 deaths, more than RM1 billion in property damage, about 2,000 homes lost, outbreaks of disease, and damage to schools and water treatment plants. Its recommendations fall into three groups. Prevention: stronger river-basin management, a review of land use, enforcement of legislation and by-laws, protection of water catchments, and a disaster risk reduction programme. Recovery: clear government policy, community engagement, volunteers, education, and a dedicated engineering corps for waterworks, in line with the Hyogo Framework for Action 2005–2015. Innovation: keep drinking water available during floods, research portable treatment systems, design water intakes for 1-in-50 or 1-in-100-year flood levels, and provide boreholes with standby generators in evacuation areas.

title: Tugu peringatan banjir Kuala Krai dan paras air 2014
chunk: Sebuah tugu peringatan banjir dibina di persimpangan lampu isyarat Guchil, Kuala Krai, untuk mengenang banjir 'bah kuning' 2014 yang dianggap terbesar dalam tempoh 50 tahun. Tugu ini dibina oleh Jupem bersama RISM, Majlis Daerah Kuala Krai dan Pejuta, dan dirasmikan oleh bekas Menteri Besar Kelantan, Datuk Ahmad Yakob, pada 28 Ogos 2016. Ia menanda paras air banjir besar di Kuala Krai: 31.31 meter pada 1931, 32.03 meter pada 1979, dan 34.17 meter pada 2014, yang tertinggi pernah direkodkan. Tugu juga menyenaraikan banjir besar pada 1926 (bah merah), 1931, 1967, 1979, 2004 dan 2014. Menurut laporan Sinar Harian, lebih 7,000 penduduk Kuala Krai menjadi mangsa banjir 2014, kira-kira 100 kediaman di Guchil dihanyutkan arus deras, dan banyak harta benda, jalan serta kemudahan awam musnah. Laporan itu menyebut paras tertinggi dicatat pada 28 Disember 2014, manakala rekod JPS mencatatkan 25 Disember.

title: Destruction in Kuala Krai villages after the 2014 flood
chunk: Malay Mail reported on 31 December 2014 that the destruction in several Kuala Krai villages was so severe that residents compared it to an attack by the mythical garuda, or to the 2004 tsunami. In Kampung Sungai Durian, which was submerged on 23 December, several houses collapsed completely and families moved to evacuation centres; one mother of three described water up to the roof of her house and was sheltering at SK Sungai Embak. Conditions were similar in Kampung Hutan Batu Balai, where residents collected food aid. A villager said his settlement was almost completely cut off by floodwater, aid had to arrive by helicopter, and houses were submerged to the roof, something not seen there for a long time. In Kuala Krai town itself, a refrigerator was left stranded on the roof of a restaurant.

title: Kuala Krai Hospital during the 2014 flood
chunk: During the December 2014 floods, Kuala Krai Hospital was cut off and also served as a temporary relief centre for flood victims. According to the Wikipedia article on the 2014–2015 Malaysian floods, the hospital lost electricity when its diesel generator ran out of fuel; staff had to intubate a baby in the dark, and patients were evacuated by helicopter. Around 180 hospital staff worked continuously for more than five days. In Kubang Kerian, the university hospital HUSM faced a blood shortage, and medical students were mobilised to support doctors on duty. The episode shows why evacuation planning must cover critical facilities as well as villages: hospitals, generators and fuel supply need to be reachable or self-sufficient when roads around Kuala Krai are flooded.

title: Manik Urai: villagers sheltering on the hills, December 2014
chunk: Malay Mail reported on 30 December 2014 that the largest floods in living memory hit Manik Urai Lama, in Kuala Krai district, around 23 December, when the overflowing Sungai Lebir drove villagers out of their homes. Many sheltered at the SM Manik Urai Lama school; others climbed into the woods and built makeshift shelters. The water peaked along the hillside of Kampung Bukit Kajang, where families took in displaced neighbours. One resident described having to keep moving higher as the water rose, staying two days in the hills, and his mother's house was destroyed. Cars were overturned at the bridge to the newer Manik Urai Baru township, which would normally have been the short route to higher ground. Villagers rationed rice and grain until the water receded. Kuala Krai's relief centres then held 4,864 evacuees.

title: Manik Urai: penduduk berlindung di bukit, Disember 2014
chunk: Menurut laporan Malay Mail pada 30 Disember 2014, banjir terbesar dalam ingatan penduduk melanda Manik Urai Lama, daerah Kuala Krai, sekitar 23 Disember apabila Sungai Lebir melimpah. Ramai penduduk berlindung di sekolah SM Manik Urai Lama, manakala yang lain mendaki ke dalam hutan dan membina tempat berteduh sementara. Air mencapai kemuncak di lereng bukit Kampung Bukit Kajang, di mana keluarga di sana menumpangkan jiran yang kehilangan tempat tinggal. Seorang penduduk berkata mereka terpaksa terus bergerak ke tempat lebih tinggi ketika air naik dan tinggal dua hari di bukit. Kereta terbalik di jambatan ke pekan baharu Manik Urai Baru, laluan singkat yang biasanya digunakan untuk ke kawasan tinggi. Penduduk mencatu beras dan bijirin sehingga air surut. Pusat pemindahan di Kuala Krai ketika itu menempatkan 4,864 mangsa.

title: Peak discharge of the Sungai Kelantan in December 2014 (HEC-HMS study)
chunk: A study in the Journal of the Civil Engineering Forum simulated the December 2014 Kelantan flood with the HEC-HMS hydrological model. It reports that the water levels of three rivers rose above their dangerous levels: the Sungai Galas at Dabong, the Sungai Lebir at Tualang and the Sungai Kelantan at Jambatan Guillemard. The simulated peak discharge was about 18,575.7 cubic metres per second, with peak discharges and inundation around 25 December 2014; the authors say this is of almost similar magnitude to the figures in the DID (JPS) 2014 flood report. For comparison, coarse global models such as GloFAS show a much lower peak for the same event, which is why MonsoonWatch labels its GloFAS-based replay as an approximation that underestimates the 2014 flood.

title: Scale of evacuation in Kelantan, late December 2014
chunk: The Star reported on 29 December 2014 that the flood situation in Kelantan had worsened, with 151,072 evacuees on Monday 29 December, up from 134,139 the night before. In total 36,128 families were affected, and 309 relief centres were open across eight districts, according to the State Social Welfare Department director, Nik Omar Nik Abdul Rahman. The numbers rose by about 17,000 people in a single night, showing how quickly relief-centre capacity can be overwhelmed when several rivers flood at once. For an early-warning system, this is why capacity checks matter: centres fill up within hours, so alerts should send villages to centres that still have space and are above the expected water level, and split large villages across more than one centre when needed.

title: Kelantan's 'bah kuning' floods: displacement and governance
chunk: In a 2019 commentary for Channel NewsAsia, republished by PreventionWeb, Serina Abdul Rahman described Kelantan's recurring monsoon floods, which locals call 'bah kuning' (yellow flood) because the water carries so much mud. Major floods hit the state in 1927 and 1967. The 2014 flood was Malaysia's worst that year and hit Kelantan hardest: about 202,000 people in the state were displaced and 13 died. The then Prime Minister was on holiday abroad and did not declare a state of emergency on his return, and civil society groups mobilised to bring food and clean water to stranded residents. The commentary argues that natural flood protection had been stripped by mining and plantations, and that distrust between the state and federal governments makes disaster relief and conservation harder.

title: Timeline of the 2014 flood in Kelantan
chunk: The Wikipedia article on the 2014–2015 Malaysian floods gives an outline timeline for Kelantan. Heavy rain from 17 December 2014 forced 3,390 people in the state to leave their homes. By 23 December most rivers in Kelantan had reached dangerous levels, and on 25 December the situation was worsening as heavy rain continued. Kelantan had the most evacuees of any state and the article cites about 354,800 people affected. Most roads in the state were closed; the state assembly building was waterlogged from 25 December; and East Coast intercity train services were disrupted from 18 December. Some flood victims crossed the Golok River into Sungai Kolok, Thailand, to buy supplies. Nationally the floods caused 21 deaths, and on 31 December a police helicopter crashed during a patrol in Kelantan.

title: How Malaysia manages flood disasters: MKN Directive No. 20
chunk: In an April 2015 parliamentary reply about the previous monsoon season's floods, the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department, Shahidan Kassim, said damage to private property and public infrastructure was estimated at RM2.9 billion. All agencies follow MKN Directive No. 20, the National Disaster Management Policy and Mechanism, which sets up disaster committees at district, state and national level; the government said it remained relevant. When the Meteorological Department issues an early warning, the Social Welfare Department (JKM) prepares evacuation centres and stocks seven days of food at 513 forward bases, with 1,069 identified suppliers for food and basic needs. JKM also provides collapsible partitions and tents to create separate areas for vulnerable groups inside evacuation centres. The flood standard operating procedure was to be reviewed for extreme floods and rapid rises.

title: Pengurusan bencana banjir: Arahan MKN No. 20 dan pangkalan hadapan
chunk: Dalam jawapan Parlimen pada April 2015, Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri menyatakan kerugian harta persendirian dan infrastruktur awam akibat banjir musim tengkujuh dianggarkan RM2.9 bilion. Semua agensi berpandukan Arahan MKN No. 20, Dasar dan Mekanisme Pengurusan Bencana Negara, yang menubuhkan jawatankuasa pengurusan bencana di peringkat daerah, negeri dan pusat. Selepas Jabatan Meteorologi mengeluarkan amaran awal, Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM) menyediakan pusat pemindahan sementara (PPS) dan menyimpan bekalan makanan untuk tujuh hari di 513 pangkalan hadapan, dengan 1,069 pembekal dikenal pasti untuk menghantar makanan dan keperluan asas. JKM juga menyediakan partition dan khemah mudah alih bagi mewujudkan ruang khas untuk golongan rentan di PPS. Prosedur operasi standard pengurusan banjir akan dikaji semula untuk menghadapi banjir luar biasa dan kenaikan air yang pantas.

title: Improving evacuation centres after the 2014–15 floods
chunk: Answering a question in Parliament in April 2015 about weaknesses at flood evacuation centres, the government said the Social Welfare Department (JKM) is responsible for flood victims under MKN Directive No. 20. After a special Disaster Management Committee meeting, JKM upgraded its evacuation centre services: collapsible partitions and tents for privacy, refreshment kits, cooked food during the first two days, an appointed manager for every centre, seven operational committees per centre, 101 psychology officers for counselling, and activities for different age groups. JKM spent RM12.94 million on the response: RM9.21 million on evacuation centre needs across the states, and RM3.73 million on emergency food, supplies and vehicle rental. For MonsoonWatch, this is the after-approval side that the Saint coordinator supports: tracking centre headcounts and supplies once an evacuation starts.

title: Banjir Disember 2023: Sungai Kelantan di Kuala Krai melepasi paras bahaya
chunk: Berita RTM melaporkan pada malam 25 Disember 2023 bahawa tiga sungai di Kelantan melepasi paras bahaya. Bacaan paras air ialah 26.6 meter bagi Sungai Kelantan di Kuala Krai, 26.8 meter bagi Sungai Nal di Kuala Krai, dan 11.01 meter bagi Sungai Golok di Rantau Panjang. Setakat jam 11 malam, sebanyak 79 pusat pemindahan sementara (PPS) dibuka di Kelantan, menempatkan 11,959 penduduk daripada 3,674 keluarga. Pada masa yang sama Terengganu membuka 95 PPS dan Pahang 14 PPS. Paras 26.6 meter di Kuala Krai jauh lebih rendah daripada rekod 34.17 meter pada 2014, tetapi tetap melebihi paras bahaya, menunjukkan banjir di Lembangan Sungai Kelantan berulang hampir setiap musim tengkujuh.

title: Sungai Golok di Rantau Panjang melepasi paras banjir 2014
chunk: Satu laporan berdasarkan data Public Info Banjir JPS dan Sinar Harian menyatakan paras air Sungai Golok di Rantau Panjang mencecah 10.97 meter pada jam 9 malam, melepasi paras bahaya. Bacaan itu 0.13 meter lebih tinggi daripada 10.84 meter yang dicatat ketika banjir 'bah kuning' 2014. Pada masa yang sama, enam lagi sungai di Kelantan melepasi paras bahaya, lima melepasi paras amaran dan lapan melepasi paras waspada. Ini menunjukkan bahawa di Lembangan Sungai Golok, paras banjir 2014 bukan lagi had tertinggi, dan sistem amaran perlu menggunakan bacaan semasa serta paras bahaya setiap stesen, bukan sekadar membandingkan dengan peristiwa lalu.

title: Gua Musang: early evacuation as Sungai Galas nears danger level (2025)
chunk: Malay Mail reported on 27 November 2025 that police in Gua Musang told residents of low-lying and riverside areas, including Kampung Limau Kasturi, to evacuate early because the Sungai Galas had reached its warning level and was feared to be approaching danger level. The Gua Musang district police chief, Supt Sik Choon Foo, said police had briefed residents and urged reluctant ones to move. A temporary evacuation centre was opened at Sekolah Kebangsaan Limau Kasturi, with the Fire and Rescue Department, the Civil Defence Force and volunteers helping. This is the pattern MonsoonWatch supports: act on the warning level before the danger level is crossed, name the villages and the centre, and give people time to move, especially elderly, disabled and bedridden residents who need help.
